evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: we talked to a lot of people everyday and most of them have one or two concerns either mover is not showing up or damaging their items are either of those a concern for you
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: customer said 'Yeah a little have enough stuff damage join' — rep replied with damage coverage details instead of 'tell me more about that' or probing deeper into the stated concern
evidence_quotes.value_days: rep offered Sunday at $192/hour instead of $200, stated savings as hourly rate ($8/hour) not total dollar amount, then asked flexibility; customer declined Saturday requirement
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: rep never mentioned rate lock or no deposit; customer asked about quote validity ('how long is this quote available for'), rep gave vague response ('before your move date') but never circled back with a commitment; no explicit ask for business, rep pivoted to email and callback

top_strength: Jeline gathered comprehensive logistics details across two pickup locations and the delivery address, including property type, floor access, distances, parking, and storage unit configuration — all critical for accurate estimating.
coaching_note: You need to ask 'How do you feel about that?' after presenting the estimate and hold the silence; you also skipped the final concerns check entirely and never actually asked for the business — both are critical bookend moments that close the sale.
